She currently practises at Fortis Hospital in Noida, where her work remains centred on radiation-based cancer treatment and on selecting an appropriate technique for each patient.

dr-christopher-john.bio:
Dr. Christopher John is a Visiting Consultant in Radiation Oncology at Rela Hospital, Chennai, with more than 14 years of experience. Neuro-oncology and head and neck oncology are his principal clinical interests, and he contributes to multidisciplinary cancer care while maintaining a defined radiation oncology role.

His radiation expertise includes stereotactic radiosurgery, stereotactic radiotherapy and stereotactic body radiation therapy, image-guided radiation therapy, brachytherapy and CyberKnife radiosurgery.

Dr. John completed his MBBS between 2006 and 2012 at Chettinad Hospital and Research Institute, Kelambakkam, under The Tamil Nadu Dr. MGR Medical University. He then took an MD in Radiotherapy from 2013 to 2016 at Vydehi Institute of Medical Sciences and Research Centre under the Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Health Science in Karnataka. At Rela Hospital he works within the Cancer Centre's radiation oncology department.

His research is PubMed indexed and follows his clinical interests closely. A 2021 paper in Contemp Oncol examined the prognostic significance of metabolic tumour volume and maximum standard uptake value of fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography with computed tomography in nasopharyngeal carcinoma. A 2021 paper in Cureus reported a retrospective analysis of concurrent taxol-based doublet chemotherapy as an alternative for intracavitary brachytherapy boost in locally advanced carcinoma cervix, and a 2018 paper in Asian Pac J Cancer Prev assessed the therapeutic benefit of placentrex in acute chemo radiation induced mucositis in oral cancer patients.

He is a member of the Association of Radiation Oncologist of India and the European Society for Radiotherapy and Oncology.

dr-rakesh-jalali.bio:
Dr. Rakesh Jalali is a Senior Consultant in Radiation Oncology at Apollo Proton Cancer Centre, Chennai, with more than 30 years of experience. Neuro-oncology and proton therapy are the most prominent areas of his work, and his clinical scope also includes radiation treatment for retinoblastoma.

He uses proton beam therapy alongside several photon-based techniques, including intensity-modulated radiation therapy, image-guided radiation therapy, 3D conformal radiotherapy and external beam radiotherapy, as well as stereotactic radiosurgery, stereotactic body radiation therapy and CyberKnife radiosurgery. His practice also covers chemotherapy for solid tumors. Having both proton and advanced photon options in one centre is what allows the modality itself to become part of the treatment decision.

After completing his MBBS, Dr. Jalali earned an MD in Radiotherapy. Before joining Apollo Proton Cancer Centre he served at Tata Memorial Hospital. He helped establish the Indian Society of Neuro-Oncology and was its founding general secretary, and his work has included developing radiation oncology guidelines and cancer care protocols.

His publications have appeared in journals including The Lancet Oncology, JAMA Oncology and the Journal of Clinical Oncology. He was named Best Oncologist by Medscape in 2014 and received the Top Radiation Oncologist Award for three consecutive years from 2014 onwards.

dr-shilpareddy-keesara.bio:
Dr. Shilpareddy Keesara is a Senior Registrar and Consultant in Radiation Oncology at Apollo Hospital, Jubilee Hills, Hyderabad, with more than 10 years of experience. Her clinical scope includes radiation treatment for retinoblastoma and radiation oncology support within brain tumour care, while her academic work has centred on prostate cancer.

She works with 3D conformal radiotherapy, intensity-modulated radiation therapy, image-guided radiation therapy and external beam radiotherapy, and her expertise also covers stereotactic body radiation therapy and stereotactic radiosurgery alongside intracavitary and interstitial brachytherapy. Between them, these techniques span conventionally fractionated treatment, highly focused radiation delivered in a few sessions, and radiation given from a source positioned in or near the area being treated.

Dr. Keesara completed her MBBS and a DNB in Radiation Oncology, with her DNB training at NIMS in Hyderabad. She subsequently served as a senior registrar at Apollo Cancer Institute and gained international exposure as a clinical observer.

Her feasibility study of hypofractionated radiotherapy in localised carcinoma prostate was presented twice in 2014 and won at both meetings: first prize at the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India conference in Imphal, and first prize in the genitourinary session at YROC in Vizag. Hypofractionation, the subject of that work, delivers a course of treatment in fewer and larger doses — a practical consideration for patients travelling for prostate cancer care.

dr-rajeev-g.bio:
Dr. Rajeev G is a Consultant in Radiation Oncology at Apollo Hospitals, Bannerghatta Road, Bengaluru, with more than 15 years of experience. His clinical interests include brain, head and neck, prostate and gynecologic cancers.

His external beam practice covers 3D conformal radiotherapy, intensity-modulated radiation therapy, image-guided radiation therapy and standard external beam radiotherapy. He also works with stereotactic radiosurgery, stereotactic body radiation therapy and CyberKnife radiosurgery, and for patients whose treatment calls for radiation delivered close to or within the tumour site, his expertise extends to intracavitary and interstitial brachytherapy. Having both conventional and highly focused options available is what allows the approach to be matched to the cancer site rather than the other way round.

Dr. Rajeev earned an MBBS and an MS, and subsequently completed a Master of Hospital Administration. That combination of clinical qualification and formal training in healthcare administration is an unusual one in radiation oncology, and it sits alongside his consultant work at Apollo Hospitals on Bannerghatta Road in Bangalore.

In 2008 he received a Gold Record in Radiation Oncology from Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences. He is a member of the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India, which connects his practice with the national professional community in the specialty.

dr-devashish-tripathi.bio:
Dr. Devashish Tripathi is a Senior Consultant in Radiation Oncology at Indraprastha Apollo Hospital, Delhi NCR, with more than 22 years of experience.

His practice covers radiation therapy for cancer, stereotactic body radiation therapy, stereotactic radiosurgery, CyberKnife radiosurgery, brachytherapy and intraoperative radiation therapy. These span highly focused external radiation, radiosurgical approaches, and treatment delivered with placed radiation sources or during an operation. He also works with chemotherapy, targeted therapy and cancer immunotherapy, which matters for patients whose plan combines radiation with systemic treatment.

A distinctive feature of his background is how much of his specialist training is from the United Kingdom. After his MBBS he completed the Professional and Linguistic Assessments Board pathway and obtained Membership of the Royal Colleges of Physicians of the United Kingdom. He went on to the Fellowship of the Royal College of Radiologists in Oncology and holds a UK Certificate of Completion of Training in Clinical Oncology, the qualification that marks the end of specialist training in that system.

At Apollo Hospitals Indraprastha in Delhi, that preparation supports a practice built around more than two decades in oncology. His profile is particularly relevant to patients being considered for stereotactic treatment, CyberKnife radiosurgery, brachytherapy or intraoperative radiation therapy, with the technique chosen according to the clinical characteristics of the case.

dr-prashant-upadhyay.bio:
Dr. Prashant Upadhyay is a Consultant in Radiation Oncology at Apollo Hospital, Jubilee Hills, Hyderabad, with more than 17 years of experience. His practice spans external beam radiotherapy, stereotactic treatment, brachytherapy and intraoperative radiation therapy.

He works with 3D conformal radiotherapy, intensity-modulated radiation therapy and image-guided radiation therapy alongside conventional external beam treatment. His expertise also includes stereotactic body radiation therapy, stereotactic radiosurgery and CyberKnife radiosurgery, which concentrate a high dose on a small, precisely defined target. For cancers suited to internal radiation he performs intracavitary and interstitial brachytherapy, and he also delivers intraoperative radiation therapy, in which the dose is given during an operation while the tumour bed is exposed.

Dr. Upadhyay completed his MBBS and a Diploma in Medical Radiotherapy before earning the Diplomate of National Board qualification in Radiation Oncology, and he also holds FUICC. His professional background includes service as a junior consultant at Yashoda Hospital and as a senior resident at Himalyan Hospital.

He now practises at Apollo Health City in Jubilee Hills, where his work focuses on selecting and planning the radiation technique that fits each patient's clinical requirements — the choice between conformal, stereotactic, internal and intraoperative delivery being driven by the site, size and stage of the tumour.

dr-amal-roy-chaudhoory.bio:
Dr. Amal Roy Chaudhoory is Senior Director of Radiation Oncology at Fortis Memorial Research Institute, Delhi NCR, with more than 25 years of experience.

His expertise spans 3D conformal radiotherapy, intensity-modulated radiation therapy, image-guided radiation therapy and external beam radiotherapy, together with stereotactic body radiation therapy, stereotactic radiosurgery and CyberKnife radiosurgery. His brachytherapy experience includes both intracavitary and interstitial techniques, and intraoperative radiation therapy, in which the dose is delivered during an operation, is also among his areas of expertise.

Taken together, that range covers conventional external beam treatment, conformal and image-guided planning, focused stereotactic radiation, internally delivered brachytherapy and radiation given in theatre. For a patient, the practical value of that breadth is that the technique can be selected on clinical grounds rather than by what a single service happens to offer.

Dr. Chaudhoory completed both his MBBS and his MD in Radiotherapy at Kasturba Medical College, Manipal. His career has since included appointments at Rajiv Gandhi Cancer Institute and at Max Hospital in Saket and Shalimarbagh, before his current senior leadership role at Fortis Hospital in Gurgaon. That path through several of the region's major cancer services sits behind the departmental responsibility he now holds, alongside his continuing clinical work in radiation oncology.

dr-g-k-jadhav.bio:
Dr. G K Jadhav is Senior Consultant and Clinical Advisor in Radiation Oncology at Indraprastha Apollo Hospital, Delhi NCR, with more than 35 years of experience. His clinical interests cover breast and prostate cancers, recurrent cancers, benign and malignant brain tumors, head and neck cancers, gynecological malignancies, and tumors of the lung, liver and spine.

His radiation practice includes stereotactic radiosurgery, stereotactic body radiation therapy, image-guided radiation therapy and adaptive radiotherapy. He works with both fractionated and hypofractionated approaches in breast and prostate cancer, and uses stereotactic treatment for selected tumors of the brain and at extracranial sites.

Dr. Jadhav holds a DNB in Radiation Oncology and completed a Commonwealth Universities fellowship in the United Kingdom as well as a UICC fellowship in the United States, alongside further training abroad in newer techniques and technology. Before joining Indraprastha Apollo he was senior faculty at Kasturba Medical College, Manipal.

Alongside clinical practice he has been principal investigator for various global clinical trials in neuro-oncology and has published in peer-reviewed national and international journals. He serves as a DNB coordinator and examiner, and has acted as advisory expert for a new greenfield oncology project in Kenya. His professional associations include AROI, AMPI and ICRO.

dr-kamal-verma.bio:
Dr. Kamal Verma is Principal Consultant in Radiation Oncology at Artemis Hospital, Delhi NCR, with more than 15 years of experience. His clinical focus includes radiotherapy for head and neck cancers, with particular interests in image-guided radiation therapy and PET-based radiotherapy planning, where imaging is used to define the target before treatment begins.

He works with 3D conformal radiotherapy, intensity-modulated radiation therapy and external beam radiotherapy, as well as stereotactic body radiation therapy and stereotactic radiosurgery. His brachytherapy practice includes both intracavitary and interstitial techniques, and he also contributes to multidisciplinary cancer care alongside medical oncology.

Dr. Verma received his MBBS from Pt. BDS PGIMS in Rohtak, Haryana, before completing a Diploma in Medical Radiotherapy and a DNB in Radiation Oncology.

His career has an international dimension that is unusual among radiation oncologists practising in Delhi NCR. Following senior residency at Maulana Azad Medical College in Delhi, he worked at the National Cancer Institute in Sabratha, Libya, and at Princess Marina Hospital in Gaborone, Botswana, where his responsibilities included cancer treatment and contributions to national cancer control programmes. He now practises at Artemis Hospitals in Gurugram, where he is a member of the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India and continues to work across head and neck radiotherapy, stereotactic treatment and brachytherapy.

dr-vineet-nakra.bio:
Dr. Vineet Nakra is a Consultant Radiation Oncologist at Fortis Hospital, Noida, Delhi NCR, with more than 9 years of experience in radiation oncology.

His external beam practice is built on the advanced techniques now standard in curative radiotherapy: 3D conformal radiotherapy, image-guided radiation therapy and intensity-modulated radiation therapy, alongside conventional external beam radiotherapy. These differ in how closely the dose is shaped to the tumour and how far imaging is used to confirm the target position before each treatment.

He also works with stereotactic body radiation therapy and stereotactic radiosurgery, which concentrate a high dose on a small, well-defined target over a small number of sessions rather than spreading it across several weeks. Within specialised radiosurgery his practice extends to CyberKnife radiosurgery and Gamma Knife radiosurgery.

His brachytherapy experience covers intracavitary and interstitial techniques, in which the radiation source is placed inside a body cavity or within the tissue itself, close to the area being treated.

Dr. Nakra holds an MBBS and a DNB, and is an MNAMS, denoting membership of the National Academy of Medical Sciences in Radiation Oncology. He also practises at Fortis Hospital, Okhla, in New Delhi. Patients considering treatment will find a practice that covers conformal, image-guided, stereotactic, radiosurgical and internally delivered radiation within one consultant service.

dr-satyesh-nadella.bio:
Dr. Satyesh Nadella is a Consultant Radiation Oncologist at Apollo Hospital, Jubilee Hills, Hyderabad, with more than 10 years of experience. His clinical background includes pediatric tumors, thoracic malignancies and gynecological malignancies, along with work in medical emergencies, professional education, and hospital safety and quality activities.

His radiation practice covers 3D conformal radiotherapy, intensity-modulated radiation therapy, image-guided radiation therapy and external beam radiotherapy. He also works with stereotactic body radiation therapy and stereotactic radiosurgery, which are used for carefully selected targets that call for highly focused delivery, and his brachytherapy expertise includes intracavitary and interstitial techniques.

Dr. Nadella earned his MBBS and an MD in Radiotherapy. Earlier in his career he was a senior resident at Mehdi Nawaz Jung Institute of Oncology and Regional Cancer Center, and he subsequently served as a senior registrar at Apollo Cancer Institutes in Jubilee Hills before moving into his current consultant role at Apollo Health City.

His academic record includes two awards from the ACCP October 2004 meeting: a best case presentation award for adenocarcinoma masquerading as neurofibroma in a patient with von Recklinghausen’s disease, and a best poster in category award for work on the role of transbronchial lung biopsy in HIV positive patients suspected to have Pneumocystis carinii pneumonia.

dr-m-vinay-ural.bio:
Dr. M Vinay Ural is a Senior Consultant in Radiation Oncology at Apollo Hospitals, Bannerghatta Road, Bengaluru, with more than 22 years of experience. His clinical interests include brain tumors, head and neck tumors, breast cancer, gynecological cancers and urogenital cancers, with a particular focus on stereotactic radiation treatments.

His expertise spans stereotactic radiosurgery and stereotactic body radiation therapy, intensity-modulated radiation therapy and image-guided radiation therapy, along with 3D conformal radiotherapy and external beam radiotherapy. His brachytherapy experience covers both intracavitary and interstitial approaches. That combination gives him a technical range running from conformal external treatment and image-guided planning through focused stereotactic techniques to internal radiation therapy.

Dr. Ural holds an MBBS, an MD in Radiation Oncology, a Diploma in Medical Radiotherapy and a DNB in Radiation Oncology — an unusually complete set of Indian radiotherapy qualifications.

He further developed his expertise through clinical training at KTH Clinical School in Leuven, Belgium, a programme focused on image-guided radiotherapy and intensity-modulated radiotherapy. Those are precisely the techniques concerned with shaping the dose to the tumour and confirming its position before delivery, and they underpin the stereotactic work that is central to his practice at Apollo Hospitals on Bannerghatta Road in Bengaluru, where he treats the brain, head and neck, breast, gynecological and urogenital cancers that make up the bulk of his caseload.

dr-divya-gupta.bio:
Dr. Divya Gupta is a Senior Consultant in Radiation Oncology at Sarvodaya Hospital, Faridabad, Delhi NCR, with more than 17 years of experience. Brain tumours are the focus of her clinical work, supported by dedicated fellowship training in the field.

Her radiotherapy expertise encompasses intensity-modulated and image-guided treatment, stereotactic radiosurgery, stereotactic body radiation therapy, volumetric modulated arc therapy, brachytherapy and total body irradiation. She also has experience with CyberKnife and Gamma Knife radiosurgery, PET-based radiation planning, electron therapy and 4D gating. The last of these accounts for tumour movement during breathing, and together with PET-based planning it belongs to the part of radiotherapy concerned with defining and tracking the target accurately — which matters most for the intracranial and stereotactic work at the centre of her practice.

Dr. Gupta completed her MBBS and her MD in Radiation Oncology at Indira Gandhi Medical College, Shimla. She then undertook a fellowship in brain tumours at Tata Memorial Hospital, Mumbai, adding focused neuro-oncology experience to her broader radiation training.

She practises at Sarvodaya Hospital, Sector 8, Faridabad, and is a life member of the Association of Radiation Oncologists of India. Her professional activity also includes research and clinical trial involvement alongside her clinical responsibilities.

dr-sapna-nangia.bio:
Dr. Sapna Nangia is a Senior Consultant in Radiation Oncology at Apollo Proton Cancer Centre, Chennai, with more than 33 years of experience.

She works with proton beam therapy as well as photon-based techniques including intensity-modulated radiation therapy, image-guided radiation therapy, 3D conformal radiotherapy and external beam radiotherapy. Her stereotactic expertise covers stereotactic body radiation therapy, stereotactic radiosurgery and CyberKnife radiosurgery, and she also performs intracavitary and interstitial brachytherapy, which deliver radiation from a source positioned within or close to the treatment area.

Having proton and photon options available in the same centre is the practical distinction in her practice: the modality itself becomes part of the treatment decision rather than a fixed starting point, and the choice can be made against the site of the tumour and the tissue around it.

Dr. Nangia completed her MBBS before earning an MD in Radiotherapy and Radiation Oncology. Her professional associations also include an affiliation with Apollo Hospitals in Delhi, and she currently practises at Apollo Proton Cancer Centre in Chennai.

With more than three decades of experience across conformal, image-guided, stereotactic, proton and internally delivered radiation, her background is defined by the breadth of techniques she can bring to an individual treatment plan — a relevant consideration for patients travelling to Chennai specifically for proton therapy.

dr-deepak-gupta.bio:
Dr. Deepak Gupta is Associate Director of Radiation Oncology at Medanta – The Medicity, Delhi NCR, with more than 17 years of experience. His clinical focus covers head and neck cancers, hepatobiliary cancers and adult lymphomas — three groups where the position of the target and its proximity to healthy tissue shape the choice of technique.

He works with stereotactic body radiation therapy and stereotactic radiosurgery, volumetric modulated arc therapy, image-guided radiation therapy, intensity-modulated radiation therapy, 3D conformal radiotherapy and external beam radiotherapy.

Dr. Gupta holds an MBBS and an MD in Radiation Oncology, along with a Post-Doctoral Certificate in Clinical Research. His professional background includes Tata Memorial Hospital in Mumbai as well as his current appointment at Medanta in Gurugram, so his experience spans a national cancer centre and a large private tertiary hospital.

His honours reflect the research side of that training. In 2014 he received the ESTRO Accuray Award from the European Society for Radiotherapy and Oncology in collaboration with Accuray, recognising excellence in radiation therapy research and practice, and in 2016 he received a travel grant from the European Society for Medical Oncology. As associate director he combines those organ-specific clinical interests with experience across conformal, image-guided and stereotactic approaches.

dr-neha-kakkar.bio:
Dr. Neha Kakkar is a Consultant in Radiation Oncology at Fortis Memorial Research Institute, Delhi NCR, with more than 12 years of experience.

Her radiation practice includes stereotactic radiosurgery and extracranial stereotactic body radiation therapy, in which a high dose is concentrated on a small, well-defined target over a few sessions. Alongside these she works with image-guided radiation therapy and intensity-modulated radiation therapy, where the dose is shaped to the tumour and its position confirmed against imaging, as well as 3D conformal radiotherapy and conventional external beam radiotherapy. She also performs intracavitary and interstitial brachytherapy, placing the radiation source within a cavity or directly into tissue close to the area being treated.

Dr. Kakkar holds an MBBS and an MD with postgraduate specialization in Radiation Oncology. Before joining Fortis Memorial Research Institute in Gurgaon she worked at Safdarjung Hospital in New Delhi and at Max Super Speciality Hospital, Saket, so her experience covers both public sector and multispecialty cancer services — a useful background when treatment has to be coordinated across different systems of care.

Alongside clinical practice she takes part in radiation oncology education and research, and her work has appeared in indexed national and international journals alongside her consultant practice at Fortis Memorial Research Institute.

dr-s-usha.bio:
Dr. S. Usha is a Radiation Oncologist at Rela Hospital, Chennai, with more than 14 years of experience. Her work with solid tumors has a particular focus on breast and gynecologic cancers, including cancers of the cervix, vagina and vulva.

Her radiation oncology expertise includes brachytherapy, stereotactic body radiation therapy, image-guided radiation therapy and total body irradiation. Within brachytherapy she has experience with intracavitary applications and implants, techniques that place the radiation source in or close to the treatment area. That is directly relevant to her gynecologic practice, where brachytherapy often forms part of the radiation plan rather than an optional addition to it. Her practice also extends to hormone therapy for breast cancer and for gynecologic cancers, so the systemic and radiation sides of treatment can be considered together.

Dr. Usha completed both her MBBS and her Diploma in Medical Radiotherapy at Madras Medical College in Chennai. She later completed a course in palliative medicine through the Indian Association of Palliative Care, and that training complements her radiotherapy practice by supporting symptom-focused care for people with advanced illness.

She practises in the Cancer Centre and Radiation Oncology Department at Rela Institute & Medical Centre in Chennai, where her listed specialisations cover both radiation oncology and medical oncology.

dr-mathangi-j.bio:
Dr. Mathangi J is Senior Consultant and In-Charge of Radiation Oncology at Gleneagles Hospitals, Bengaluru, with more than 19 years of experience. She is based at Gleneagles BGS Hospital in Kengeri and holds MBBS, DMRT and DNB qualifications.

Her practice encompasses radiation therapy for cancer and brachytherapy together with several specialised external beam techniques. She has experience in image-guided and intensity-modulated radiation therapy, stereotactic body radiation therapy and stereotactic radiosurgery, and CyberKnife radiosurgery is a further part of her technical scope.

Two less common techniques extend that range in useful directions. She works with total body irradiation, in which radiation is delivered across the whole body for specific clinical indications, and with intraoperative radiation therapy, where the dose is given during an operation while the tumour bed is exposed. Both sit alongside her focused stereotactic work and her brachytherapy practice, in which the radiation source is placed within or close to the area being treated rather than directed at it from outside.

Taken together, her senior departmental responsibility, her formal medical and radiotherapy qualifications and her experience across external, focused, internal, intraoperative and whole-body radiation reflect a career centred on radiation oncology and on matching the delivery method to the clinical situation in front of her.

dr-sapna-manocha-verma.bio:
Dr. Sapna Manocha Verma is a Senior Consultant in Radiation Oncology at Indraprastha Apollo Hospital, Delhi NCR, with more than 22 years of experience.

Her radiation work includes radiation therapy for cancer, brachytherapy, stereotactic body radiation therapy and stereotactic radiosurgery. These cover the main ways a dose can be delivered: shaped from outside the body over a course of treatment, concentrated on a small defined target in a few sessions, or given from a source placed within or close to the area being treated.

What distinguishes her profile is that it extends past radiation into systemic treatment. Her practice also takes in chemotherapy for cancer, cancer immunotherapy and targeted therapy for cancer, so the drug and radiation components of a plan can be considered together rather than referred separately.

A third strand is hormone-based treatment, covering hormonal therapy for gynaecologic cancers and hormone therapy for breast cancer. Those two groups are where hormone-directed treatment is most often combined with radiation, and their presence in her practice points to where her clinical experience is concentrated.

Dr. Verma holds an MBBS and an MD in Radiotherapy, and practises within the radiation oncology service at Indraprastha Apollo Hospitals in Delhi, where she has spent her recent career as a senior consultant.

dr-sravanthi-reddy-t.bio:
Dr. Sravanthi Reddy T is a Consultant Radiation Oncologist at Yashoda Hospitals, Secunderabad, Hyderabad, with more than 11 years of experience. Her work has a particular focus on gynecological oncology and also incorporates pain and palliative care.

Her radiation practice includes brachytherapy, image-guided radiation therapy and stereotactic body radiation therapy alongside broader radiation therapy for cancer. Brachytherapy delivers radiation from a source positioned within or close to the treatment area, while stereotactic body radiation therapy concentrates focused external radiation on selected targets. Her practice also extends to chemotherapy for cancer and hormone therapy for gynecologic cancers, which means the systemic and radiation elements of a gynecological cancer plan can be considered side by side.

Dr. Reddy earned her MBBS at Osmania Medical College in Hyderabad and later completed her Diplomate of National Board training in the Department of Radiotherapy at Yashoda Hospitals, Somajiguda. She has since been affiliated with Yashoda Hospitals at both Somajiguda and Secunderabad, where she now practises as a consultant.

She takes part in clinico-pathological and clinico-radiological meetings, the forums where pathology, imaging and treatment teams review cases together — a routine but important part of coordinating a cancer diagnosis and the treatment that follows for the patients under her care.

dr-gowhar-ahmad-shigan.bio:
Dr. Gowhar Ahmad Shigan is a Senior Consultant in Radiation Oncology at Paras Hospitals, Gurugram, Delhi NCR, with more than 13 years of experience.

He works with stereotactic radiosurgery and stereotactic body radiation therapy, image-guided radiation therapy, intensity-modulated radiation therapy, volumetric modulated arc therapy, 3D conformal radiotherapy and external beam radiotherapy. His practice also includes intracavitary and interstitial brachytherapy, among them brachytherapy for gynaecological and other malignancies, where the radiation source is placed within or beside the tissue being treated.

That range allows treatment planning to draw on conventional external beam radiotherapy as well as highly focused stereotactic techniques and brachytherapy, according to the requirements of the individual cancer and treatment site. His experience covers the management of both common and complex cancers.

Dr. Shigan holds an MBBS and a DNB in Radiation Oncology, and during his DNB course he received the Best Resident Award in Radiation Oncology.

Alongside clinical care at Paras Health in Gurugram, he takes part in academic teaching, oncology research and the training of younger oncologists. For patients, the relevant point is a consultant practice that covers conformal, image-guided, stereotactic, external beam and brachytherapy approaches within one service, backed by continuing academic involvement in the specialty.
